---
title: "The plug-in window"
---

![](../images/screenshot.png){fig-alt="The plug-in window."}

The window has five areas: the header, the memory matrix, the side panel, the memory buttons, and the
parameter pages, with a status bar along the bottom. It can be resized from the bottom-right corner.

## Header

The preset menu with **<** and **>** to step through presets, and **Save…** to save your own
([Presets](presets.qmd)). On the right, the **MIDI** light flashes when a note arrives, and the version number.

## Memory matrix

One row per stored trace, **oldest at the top**. From left to right:

| Column | Shows |
|---|---|
| **Lock** | An amber lock if the trace is **clamped**. Click here to clamp or unclamp it. |
| **Activation** | How strongly the trace answered the last cue: amber for positive, blue for negative, scaled to the strongest. |
| **Heads 1 2 3** | Which playback heads are playing the trace right now (1 amber, 2 teal, 3 violet); brighter = louder. |
| **Address** | The trace's 384-number address exactly as MINERVA stores it: 16 time slots, left to right, each a 24-band spectrum from low to high. Amber is above the trace's average level, blue below. |

With **Sequence Context** on, each address is shown as **[n−1 | n]**: the previous segment's address, a divider,
then the trace's own ([Sequences](sequences.qmd)).

Rows are tall while memory is nearly empty and shrink as it fills, so the view always fits; the space below the
last row stands for free slots. With more traces than pixels (grain memories), each pixel row shows the
strongest of the traces it covers.

Hover over a row for its details. **Click** a row to inspect it in the side panel; click again to deselect.

The line above the matrix gives memory's fill (*traces / capacity*), how many are clamped, what happened to the
last segment (*stored*, *merged*, *gated*, *rejected (full)*, *frozen*) and how many traces the current echo uses.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Reading the matrix
Repeated material shows up as rows with similar stripes. When you play something familiar, the activation bars
light up on the rows that resemble it; with **Activation Power** high, only one or two light up; with it low,
many do.
:::

## Side panel

- **Heard**: the address of the last segment you played, which is what cued memory. Time runs left to right,
  low bands at the bottom.
- With Sequence Context on, *Heard* shows the last two segments [n−1 | n] and *Echo* shows the echo's context half
  and its *n* half, labelled "expected next" in Predict Next and Echo Chain.
- **Echo**: the echo's content, the activation-weighted blend of the answering traces' addresses (MINERVA's
  echo). Compare it with *Heard* to see how memory reinterpreted what you played.
- **Familiarity**: the strongest activation, as a bar, and MINERVA's **intensity** (the sum of activations).
- **Selected trace**: its address, age (traces stored since), length, level, strength, generation (0 = heard,
  1+ = an echo that was recorded) and how many segments were merged into it, with **Clamp**/**Unclamp** and
  **Delete** buttons.

## Memory buttons

| Button | Does |
|---|---|
| **Capture** | Store the segment in progress when it ends, even if gates or freeze would skip it. |
| **Clamp Last** | Clamp the newest trace. |
| **Clamp All** | Clamp the newest traces, up to the **Clamp Budget**. |
| **Unclamp All** | Unclamp everything. |
| **Clear Unclamped** | Forget every unclamped trace. |
| **Clear All** | Empty memory. |
| **Import Audio…** | Add audio files to memory as traces (or drop files on the window). |
| **Save Memory…** / **Load Memory…** | Save memory as a folder of WAVs plus a manifest, or load one. |
| **Clamp imports** | Clamp imported traces. |

See [Importing and saving memory](import-save.qmd).

## Parameter pages

**Main** gathers the essentials; the other pages hold everything else: **Memory**, **Forgetting**,
**Retrieval**, **Cueing**, **Heads**, **Tape**, **Spectral**, **Mix** and **Control** (MIDI and the trigger
parameters). Every parameter is described in the [parameter reference](../reference/parameters.qmd).

Controls that have no effect with the current settings are dimmed (for example **Trace Length (Free)** while
**Sync** is Tempo). Double-click a knob to reset it to its default.

## Status bar

A progress bar through the current segment, then the trace length, the host tempo and bar, the longest trace a
memory slot can hold, and counts of evictions and merges. In Rolling cue mode it shows how far behind the live
cue is. Messages from imports, saves and presets appear here for a few seconds.
